raw_response:
I will keep my main land in the wheat-maize rotation, because that is what I know best, it fits my irrigation conditions, and it gives me the most stable grain output on a large area with only two people in the household. I will put 90 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same 90 mu, because grain is still the backbone of my farm and it is easier for me to manage at scale. I will keep 25 mu in cotton because I have long experience with it and it spreads risk, but I will not expand it too much because it needs more labor and more spraying. I will plant 14 mu of millet because it is relatively hardy, does not need as much water, and gives me another crop in case grain prices or weather go against me. Since I have well irrigation, I will use water to protect yield on wheat and maize first, then keep inputs moderate on millet and controlled but steady on cotton. I will use improved or hybrid seed where it clearly helps yield and stability, and I will stay with cultivation methods that match my labor, machinery habits, and 40 years of experience.
